rationale:
Split into two children. Both are comparator-accepted declarations, reused under their existing names with frozen types copied byte-for-byte from dag.json. No new child worker is needed, and the selected node keeps only a short assembly.

Mapping to the supplied proof:
- Steps 1–3 go to gram_schmidt_frame = Submission.dpf_exists_orthonormal_frame_det_gram (accepted, candidate 93ec31ab).
  - These steps are: an orthonormal basis of V = span a; R_kl = ⟨τ_k, a_l⟩ invertible; Γ = RᵀR, so det Γ = (det R)².
  - The child's σ is the proof's τ and its A is R. Its extra conjunct |det A| ≤ ∏|v_a| is not used.
- Step 4 goes to covector_frame_det = Submission.dgoj_covector_eq_det_mul_of_mem_span (accepted, candidate 73310ec9).
  - This step is α(a) = det R·α(τ), via AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det on V.
- Step 5 is the parent's own assembly.

How the children imply the selected statement:
1. gram_schmidt_frame with v := a gives an orthonormal σ with span σ = span a, det Γ = (det R)² and det R ≠ 0, where R := (⟨σ_i, a_j⟩).
2. Since det R ≠ 0, det Γ = (det R)² > 0. This is the first conjunct.
3. Fix ξ with ξ(α) = (√det Γ)⁻¹·α(a). Each a_j lies in span a = span σ. So covector_frame_det with τ := σ and b := a gives α(a) = det R·α(σ) for every α.
4. √det Γ = √((det R)²) = |det R| (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs). So ξ(α) = |det R|⁻¹·det R·α(σ).
5. If det R > 0, then ξ(α) = α(σ) for all α. If det R < 0, then ξ(α) = −α(σ) for all α. Since σ is orthonormal with span σ = span a, this is IsUnitOrientationOf ξ (span a).
6. n = 0 needs no separate case, because both children hold for empty families.

subproblems.title: Gram–Schmidt frame of an independent family: det Gram(v) = (det A)², det A ≠ 0, |det A| ≤ ∏|v_a| (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let v = (v_1, …, v_n) (indexed by Fin n) be a linearly independent family in ℝ^P (Euclid P). Then there is an orthonormal family σ = (σ_1, …, σ_n) in ℝ^P with span{σ_1, …, σ_n} = span{v_1, …, v_n} such that, for the n×n real matrix A with entries A_{ab} := ⟨σ_a, v_b⟩: (i) det(⟨v_a, v_b⟩)_{a,b} = (det A)²; (ii) det A ≠ 0; (iii) |det A| ≤ ∏_a |v_a|. Here ⟨·,·⟩ and |·| are the Euclidean inner product and norm.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → Euclid P), LinearIndependent ℝ v → ∃ σ : Fin n → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ σ ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range σ) = Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) ∧ Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (v i) (v j)) = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (σ i) (v j)) ^ 2 ∧ Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (σ i) (v j)) ≠ 0 ∧ |Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (σ i) (v j))| ≤ ∏ i, ‖v i‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Steps 1–3 of the parent proof, stated for an arbitrary linearly independent family v. Those steps are: an orthonormal basis τ of V = span a; R_kl = ⟨τ_k, a_l⟩ invertible; ⟨a_i, a_k⟩ = (RᵀR)_ik, so det Γ = (det R)². Here the orthonormal basis is chosen by Gram–Schmidt. Conjunct (iii) is part of the frozen type but is not used by the parent; it is proved in step 7.

This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dpf_exists_orthonormal_frame_det_gram (DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.orientation_pushforward-a1.gram_schmidt_frame-a1, status accepted, candidate commit 93ec31ab). It is reused with its byte-identical frozen Lean type. Its accepted proof follows.

Notation: ⟨·,·⟩ and |·| are the Euclidean inner product and norm of ℝ^P.

1. The subspace W.
   - Let W := span{v_1, …, v_n} ⊆ ℝ^P with the restricted inner product. It is a finite-dimensional inner product space. Let ι_W : W → ℝ^P be the inclusion.
   - Since v is linearly independent, dim W = n = card(Fin n) (finrank_span_eq_card).
   - Each v_b lies in W. Let w_b ∈ W be v_b regarded as an element of W, so ι_W(w_b) = v_b.
   - w is linearly independent in W, because ι_W ∘ w = v is linearly independent (LinearIndependent.of_comp).
   - w spans W. The map ι_W sends span(w) onto span(ι_W ∘ w) = span v = W = ι_W(W) (Submodule.map_span, Set.range_comp, Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype). The induced map on submodules is injective (Submodule.map_injective_of_injective), so span(w) = W, the top submodule of W.

2. Gram–Schmidt. Apply Gram–Schmidt orthonormalisation in W to w, in the order of Fin n (InnerProductSpace.gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis, using finrank W = card(Fin n) from step 1).
   - This gives an orthonormal basis b = (b_1, …, b_n) of W.
   - Its coefficients for w are upper triangular: ⟨b_a, w_c⟩ = 0 whenever c < a (gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis_inv_triangular).
   - Hence the basis determinant of w with respect to b is the product of the diagonal entries: det_b(w) = ∏_a ⟨b_a, w_a⟩ (gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis_det; det_b is Module.Basis.det of b.toBasis).

3. The frame σ. Define σ_a := ι_W(b_a) ∈ ℝ^P.
   - Norms and inner products of elements of W are computed in ℝ^P. So |σ_a| = 1 and ⟨σ_a, σ_c⟩ = 0 for a ≠ c, i.e. σ is orthonormal (Orthonormal.comp_linearIsometry with W.subtypeₗᵢ).
   - b is a basis, so span b = W. Therefore span σ = span(ι_W ∘ b) = ι_W(span b) = ι_W(W) = W = span v (Set.range_comp, Submodule.span_image, Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype).

4. The coefficient matrix.
   - For an orthonormal basis, the a-th coordinate of w_c is ⟨b_a, w_c⟩ (OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis_repr_apply, OrthonormalBasis.repr_apply_apply).
   - Inner products in W are those of ℝ^P (Submodule.coe_inner), so ⟨b_a, w_c⟩ = ⟨σ_a, v_c⟩ = A_{ac}. Thus A is the matrix of w in the basis b (Module.Basis.toMatrix_apply).
   - Hence det A = det_b(w) (Module.Basis.det_apply) = ∏_a ⟨σ_a, v_a⟩ by step 2.

5. (i) Gram identity.
   - Fix a and c. Parseval's identity for the orthonormal basis b of W (OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner) gives ⟨v_a, v_c⟩ = ⟨w_a, w_c⟩ = Σ_k ⟨w_a, b_k⟩⟨b_k, w_c⟩.
   - By symmetry of the real inner product (real_inner_comm), this sum equals Σ_k ⟨σ_k, v_a⟩⟨σ_k, v_c⟩ = Σ_k A_{ka}A_{kc} = (AᵀA)_{ac}.
   - So (⟨v_a, v_c⟩)_{a,c} = AᵀA, and det(⟨v_a, v_c⟩) = det(Aᵀ)·det(A) = (det A)² (Matrix.det_mul, Matrix.det_transpose).

6. (ii) det A ≠ 0. By step 4, det A = det_b(w). By step 1, w is linearly independent and spans W, so det_b(w) is a unit (Module.Basis.is_basis_iff_det), hence nonzero.

7. (iii) The bound.
   - By step 4 and multiplicativity of the absolute value (Finset.abs_prod), |det A| = ∏_a |⟨σ_a, v_a⟩|.
   - For each a, Cauchy–Schwarz and |σ_a| = 1 give |⟨σ_a, v_a⟩| ≤ |σ_a|·|v_a| = |v_a| (abs_real_inner_le_norm).
   - All factors are nonnegative, so the products compare factor by factor (Finset.prod_le_prod₀): |det A| ≤ ∏_a |v_a|.

8. The case n = 0. Steps 1–7 never assume n > 0, so they cover it. All families are empty, W = {0}, A is the empty matrix with det A = 1 ≠ 0, det(⟨v_a, v_b⟩) = 1 = 1², and the empty product is 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: W := span v has dimension n; v regarded in W is a linearly independent spanning family w.
Gram–Schmidt in W gives an orthonormal basis b with det_b(w) = ∏_a ⟨b_a, w_a⟩ (upper-triangular coefficients).
σ := b regarded in ℝ^P is orthonormal, with span σ = W = span v.
A_{ac} = ⟨σ_a, v_c⟩ is the coefficient matrix of w in b, so det A = det_b(w) = ∏_a ⟨σ_a, v_a⟩.
Parseval gives (⟨v_a, v_c⟩) = AᵀA, hence det Gram(v) = (det A)².
det A = det_b(w) is a unit because w is a basis of W, so det A ≠ 0.

subproblems.title: An n-covector on vectors in the span of an orthonormal n-frame equals det(⟨τ_i, b_j⟩) times its value on the frame (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) (indexed by Fin n) be an orthonormal family in ℝᴾ = Euclid P and let b = (b₁, …, bₙ) be a family in ℝᴾ with bⱼ ∈ span{τ₁, …, τₙ} for every j. Then for every n-covector α of ℝᴾ (α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n, a continuous alternating n-linear form), α(b₁, …, bₙ) = det(𝒜)·α(τ₁, …, τₙ), where 𝒜 is the n×n real matrix 𝒜ᵢⱼ := ⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩ (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (b j)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ b : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (∀ j, b j ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ)) → ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, α b = (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (b j)).det * α τ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 4 of the parent proof, stated for an arbitrary orthonormal frame τ and any family b in its span. In that step, the restriction of α to V is an alternating n-form on the n-dimensional space V. So it equals α(τ)·det_τ (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det), and det_τ(a) = det R.

This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dgoj_covector_eq_det_mul_of_mem_span (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.epsilon_regularity-a1.graph_cycle_regular-a1.graph_orientation_jacobian-a1.covector_frame_det-a1, status accepted, candidate commit 73310ec9). It is reused with its byte-identical frozen Lean type. Its accepted proof follows.

Notation: L := span{τ₁, …, τₙ} ⊆ ℝᴾ. For c ∈ L, ↑c ∈ ℝᴾ is its underlying vector. An n-covector is an element of Covector (Euclid P) n = Euclid P [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ.

1. A basis of L indexed by Fin n. An orthonormal family is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so τ is a basis of its span. So e := Module.Basis.span hτ.linearIndependent is a basis (e₁, …, eₙ) of L with ↑eᵢ = τᵢ (Module.Basis.span_apply).

2. Restriction of α to L.
   - Let α_L := α.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap L.subtype, i.e. α_L(c₁, …, cₙ) := α(↑c₁, …, ↑cₙ) for cᵢ ∈ L. It is an alternating n-linear form on L.
   - Put b'ⱼ := ⟨bⱼ, hbⱼ⟩ ∈ L; this is allowed by the hypothesis bⱼ ∈ L.
   - Then α(b) = α_L(b'), and α(τ) = α(↑e) = α_L(e). Both hold by unfolding, using ↑eᵢ = τᵢ from step 1.

3. Basis determinant. Every alternating n-form on the n-dimensional space L with basis e is a multiple of the basis determinant: α_L = α_L(e)·det_e (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at b' gives α_L(b') = α_L(e)·det_e(b').

4. The coordinate matrix. det_e(b') = det M with Mᵢⱼ := e.repr(b'ⱼ)ᵢ (Module.Basis.det_apply, Module.Basis.toMatrix_apply). We claim Mᵢⱼ = ⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩.
   - b'ⱼ = Σₗ Mₗⱼ·eₗ (Module.Basis.sum_repr).
   - Taking underlying vectors (Submodule.coe_sum, Submodule.coe_smul, step 1) gives bⱼ = Σₗ Mₗⱼ·τₗ.
   - Taking the inner product with τᵢ and using orthonormality, ⟨τᵢ, Σₗ Mₗⱼτₗ⟩ = Mᵢⱼ (Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype).
   - Hence M = 𝒜.

5. Conclusion. Combining steps 2–4: α(b) = α_L(b') = α_L(e)·det_e(b') = α(τ)·det 𝒜 = det(𝒜)·α(τ). The argument is uniform in n. For n = 0 both sides are α of the empty family, since the empty matrix has determinant 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: τ orthonormal ⇒ linearly independent ⇒ e := Module.Basis.span is a basis of L = span τ with ↑eᵢ = τᵢ.
Restrict α to L: α_L := α.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap L.subtype, with α(b) = α_L(b') and α(τ) = α_L(e).
AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det: α_L = α_L(e)·det_e, so α(b) = α(τ)·det_e(b').
det_e(b') is the determinant of the coordinate matrix, whose (i,j) entry is ⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩ by expanding bⱼ = Σₗ cₗⱼτₗ and using orthonormality.
